title: IS12:: countdown1.c (4.1)

lines.code: Objective: practicing simple while loop with countdown control */

lines.explanation: This variable will be used as a loop counter. It is declared as integer and initialized to 5
The line Start counting will be printed before the loop

At each iteration of the loop, the current value of the counter is checked. If this value is zero (0), the loop will will be skipped, otherwise execution will proceed with the first statement inside the loop.
This statement simply prints the current value of counter.
The goal of this statement is to subtract 1 from the current value of the counter. I.e., the value of counter will be "one less".
This is the end of the block braces. We need to use block here since while statement can have only one C statement inside its body. We have two and so we need to wrap them as a block.
This is the first statement after the loop. Here the execusion will resume when checking the expression controlling the loop (counter) we will find that it became zero
